## 1) Run AUB autopilot (module-level) and select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```

### What this should do
- Loads `experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml` (your module search space / candidates).
- Runs the AUB evaluation loop over the candidate set.
- Applies your selection rule (`--select-best`) to pick the best-performing candidate and (usually) update whatever pointer/record your system uses for “current champion” at the module level.

### What to verify afterward
- A report/log indicating:
  - Which candidates were tried
  - Their metrics (especially tuning_mean/min and lockbox_mean/min or whatever AUB uses)
  - The selected best candidate
- Whether any “champion” file or symlink/reference was updated (depends on your framework conventions). If the tool prints something like “Selected best: … wrote …”, confirm the file exists.

### If it fails
Paste the stdout/stderr and the contents of:
- `experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml`
- any generated report path it references

---

## 2) Run system autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```

### What this should do
- Loads system-level candidate specs from `experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml`.
- Runs end-to-end evaluations across those system candidates (often combining modules, prompts, routing, etc.).
- Produces comparative results for system candidates. (Some setups also auto-promote, but your command doesn’t include `--select-best`, so it may only evaluate and report.)

### What to verify afterward
- A generated report with:
  - All system candidates evaluated
  - Aggregate metrics and per-slice metrics (if applicable)
  - Any gating rules / pass-fail flags

### If you want it to auto-promote
If your tool supports it, there may be a `--select-best` or `--promote` flag analogous to the AUB tool. If you want, paste `--help` output and I’ll tell you the right flag.

---

## 3) Generate “next fix” plan
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

### What this should do
- Reads the module registry and the latest eval outcomes.
- Produces a prioritized “next fix” markdown plan at:
  - `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`

### What to verify afterward
- File exists and is non-empty:
  ```bash
  ls -lah baseline/reports/next_fix.md
  sed -n '1,200p' baseline/reports/next_fix.md
  ```
- The recommendations align with the most recent runs (i.e., references the correct candidate IDs and metrics).

---

- lockbox_mean improved (usually the harder “don’t overfit” metric)
- lockbox_min doesn’t regress (often a guardrail)
- any improvement is statistically meaningful if your framework provides variance / confidence intervals

